A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfiniDreamer and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures and tables can be matched reliably despite revisions and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanML3D and BABEL evaluations, ablations and generated-motion examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative motion-generation experiments, including revised and additional results.

M1.justification: v1 explicitly uses unconditional SSD refinement. v2 introduces motion/transition gradient masks, boundary interpolation and a rule selecting textual conditions for sampled segments, reflected in Figure 2 and Algorithm 1. These substantially revise refinement. However, v2 retains the old unconditional denoising description and formula, creating an internal inconsistency.

E1.justification: Both evaluate text-conditioned motion composition and transitions on HumanML3D and BABEL, and both include the 520-frame single-prompt demonstration. Revised qualitative prompts and motion-prior configurations remain within this existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets remain unchanged in corresponding main and supplementary experiments, including DoubleTake, DiffCollage, TEACH, MultiDiffusion and FlowMDM with their existing variants. The added '+MLD' row evaluates an InfiniDreamer prior variant.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the default window size from 60 to 120 while retaining stride 30. Table 3 revises the window/stride sweep, and Table 4 introduces an MLD-prior configuration. The datasets, main metrics, 20,000 optimization iterations and learning rate remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 1–2 add gradient-mask removal ablations. Table 6 recasts the prompt study around the selection strategy, comparing generic prompts and unconditional refinement. The window/stride study and Figure 3 case studies are revised, while the learning-rate illustration and single-prompt demonstration are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten evaluation repetitions in the comparison-table captions and use the same plus/minus reporting practice. No new seed information, uncertainty definition or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Main and ablation results are substantially replaced. For example, Table 1 changes InfiniDreamer's R-precision/FID from 0.627/0.62 to 0.679/0.47 under the revised method and window setting, preventing a clean same-setting comparison. Table 4 adds MLD-variant results. The old FlowMDM-based rows largely survive as '+FlowMDM', but their previously reported PJ/AUJ entries disappear from Tables 4–5.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal prompt-selection distribution in Equation 3: select the corresponding prompt within one sub-motion, or uniformly among prompts for overlapping sub-motions. The existing SDS derivation and Appendix A's global-consistency argument, now Section 8, remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free, arbitrarily long motion generation through SSD, local and global coherence, and improvements over previous training-free methods. The rewritten abstract and conclusion retain this scope and the claimed independence from a particular motion prior.

C2.justification: v1 interprets its prompt ablation as supporting unconditional refinement. v2 instead argues that prompt selection is beneficial, unconditional refinement is suboptimal, and generic prompts inadequately represent transition semantics. The limitations concerning dependence on the short-motion model and approximately four minutes per 520-frame sequence are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies gradient-mask values of 0.1 and 0.8, updates the documented window size, and adds mask initialization and prompt selection to Algorithm 1. Existing hardware, optimization-budget, encoding, guidance-scale and runtime disclosures are retained; no new code or data access information appears.

R1.justification: Background citations are revised, including additions such as LongAnimation and VividDreamer and removals such as Noise-free Score Distillation, LucidDreamer and HIFA. Changes mainly affect supporting citation lists; the detailed positioning against prior motion-generation methods remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are rewritten, method and prompt-ablation explanations are expanded, and affiliations and acknowledgments are updated. Appendices A–D become Sections 8–11. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to show masks and conditioning, and Figure 3 replaces the qualitative examples. Tables add or reorganize variant and ablation rows, and Algorithm 1 moves from the main text to the supplement. Figures 1 and 4–6 and the overall two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The new mask ablations, revised conditioning controls and additional prior variant strengthen component-level evidence. However, v2's prompt-selection rule conflicts with its retained unconditional denoising description, and Tables 4–5 remove previously available own-method PJ/AUJ results. These gains coexist with reduced methodological consistency and transition-result completeness, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
